func_num_args() returns the number of arguments passed to the function, regardless of the declared parameters.

In PHP, the 'use' keyword captures variables by value at the time the closure is defined, so $x inside the closure remains 5 even after the outer $x is changed to 7.

Reassigning a readonly property throws an Error (specifically, a TypeError or a dedicated readonly error depending on PHP version), not an Exception.

In PHP 7 and later, the Throwable interface is indeed the base interface implemented by both Exception and Error classes.
TypeError inherits from Error, not Exception, so it is not caught by a standard catch (Exception $e) block.
The @ operator suppresses error reporting (warnings/notices) but does not prevent exceptions from being thrown or caught.
The intdiv function throws a DivisionByZeroError when the divisor is zero.
The finally block executes regardless of whether an exception was thrown, caught, or if the try block completed successfully.
An exception thrown in a finally block will override the original exception or return value from the try block.

Shutdown functions registered via register_shutdown_function() are executed when the script terminates, including when exit or die is called.

In PHP, arrays are copied by value when assigned to a new variable, so modifying $b does not affect $a.
PHP variables have function scope by default, so global variables are not accessible inside functions unless explicitly imported via the global keyword, $GLOBALS superglobal, or passed as arguments.

The function inc takes a parameter by reference (&$x), so the increment operation modifies the original variable $n directly.
In PHP, a foreach loop iterates over a copy of the array when iterating by value, so changes to the original array inside the loop do not affect the current iteration's elements.
Static properties belong to the class itself and are shared among all instances, so changes in one object are visible in others.
PHP automatically converts boolean keys to integers (true becomes 1, false becomes 0) when used as array keys.

Generators cannot be rewound once they have been fully consumed or started; calling rewind() on a generator throws an exception.
The yield from expression in PHP (available since 5.5) is used to delegate the generation of values to another generator or iterable.

The generator yields three values (1, 2, 3), which iterator_to_array converts into an array of three elements.

ArrayIterator implements the Iterator interface and allows traversing an array.
ArrayObject implements the IteratorAggregate interface, allowing it to be traversed with foreach.

In Clean and Onion Architecture, the Dependency Rule states that source code dependencies must point only inward, toward higher-level policies, meaning inner layers do not depend on outer layers.
In clean architecture, domain entities should remain framework-agnostic and depend only on the language core to ensure testability and decoupling.
Controllers and Twig templates belong to the presentation layer, not the business-logic layer.
In the onion architecture pattern, the domain model (or core business logic) is placed at the very center, surrounded by application services and then infrastructure layers.
Tools like deptrac analyze code dependencies and fail the build if forbidden layer interactions are detected.
Use cases (interactors) should be independent of frameworks and specific implementations like HTTP requests or EntityManager to maintain clean architecture principles.
In Domain-Driven Design, the Repository pattern acts as a collection-like interface for domain objects, abstracting away the underlying data storage mechanism.
Clean architecture isolates business logic from infrastructure details, allowing database swaps without affecting the domain or use cases.
In Domain-Driven Design, an aggregate is a cluster of domain objects treated as a single unit for data changes, not necessarily corresponding to a single database table.
Value Objects are defined by their state and must be immutable to ensure consistent equality comparisons based on field values rather than object identity.
In Domain-Driven Design, the root entity of an aggregate is the single external entry point through which all changes must go.
In Domain-Driven Design, repositories are specifically designed to manage the lifecycle of aggregate roots, not individual entities within an aggregate.

Ubiquitous language is a core concept in Domain-Driven Design, defined as a shared vocabulary used by both developers and domain experts to ensure clear communication and alignment with the domain model.
In model theory, an elementary substructure is a submodel where the truth of first-order formulas is preserved between the submodel and the larger model.
Domain-Driven Design (DDD) explicitly advocates for rich domain models where behavior resides within entities, rejecting the anemic model pattern as an anti-pattern.
In Domain-Driven Design, bounded contexts enforce that the same ubiquitous language term may map to different models or classes depending on the specific context.

The 'make:form' command in Symfony MakerBundle generates a new form type class.
Symfony stores the user's password hash (if using hashing) or never stores the plain text password in the session; typically, only the user identifier is stored in the session after authentication.

The 'debug:container' command lists all registered services and aliases in the Symfony DI container.

By default, Symfony services are private; they must be explicitly marked as public to be fetched directly from the container.
Symfony bundles can function without a specific config file if they rely on default configurations or auto-discovery, so configuration is not strictly mandatory for every bundle to work.
Symfony supports the %env(VAR)% syntax to inject environment variable values into service configuration files.
The APP_DEBUG environment variable controls debug mode in Symfony, enabling features like the profiler and Twig debugging.

Symfony Messenger allows adding custom middleware to the pipeline using addMiddleware, which can be configured to run before or after existing built-in middleware.

The 'number_format' filter in twig/intl-extra formats numbers according to the specified locale.

Bootstrap is primarily a front-end component library for responsive design, whereas SPA frameworks like Angular or React manage application state and routing.
The .container class provides a responsive fixed width container that adjusts its max-width at each breakpoint.
The Bootstrap grid is built on flexbox (in versions 4 and 5) or floats (in version 3), but it splits a row into 12 columns, not 16.

Doctrine ORM does not automatically create database tables at runtime; schema generation requires explicit commands like `doctrine:migrations:generate` or `doctrine:schema:update`.
The persist method adds a new entity to the managed state, but no SQL INSERT is generated until flush() is called.

DQL (Doctrine Query Language) operates on object entities and their mapped fields, abstracting away the underlying database tables and columns.

In Doctrine ORM, remove() only marks the entity for deletion; the actual SQL DELETE is executed during flush().
PostgreSQL's MVCC implementation allows readers and writers to operate concurrently without blocking each other.
The EXPLAIN keyword is used in SQL to display the execution plan of a statement without running it.

SERIAL is a PostgreSQL-specific shorthand for creating an integer column with a sequence, while GENERATED AS IDENTITY is the SQL standard way to define identity columns, and they have different underlying mechanisms and behaviors.
In PostgreSQL, NULL values are considered distinct from each other in UNIQUE constraints, allowing multiple rows with NULL.
The string_agg function is used to concatenate strings with a specified separator.
Plain VACUUM does not return space to the operating system; it only marks dead tuples as reusable within the table, whereas VACUUM FULL is required to release space back to the OS.
The PARTITION BY keyword in a window function definition divides the result set into partitions, over which the function is computed.
READ COMMITTED allows non-repeatable reads; REPEATABLE READ is the isolation level that protects against them.
PostgreSQL operates in autocommit mode by default, treating each individual SQL statement as a separate transaction unless explicitly grouped with BEGIN/COMMIT.
The COMMIT statement permanently saves all changes made during the current transaction to the database.
Indexes accelerate data retrieval for UPDATE and DELETE statements by allowing the database to quickly locate specific rows without scanning the entire table.
PostgreSQL uses SAVEPOINT to mark a point within a transaction that can be rolled back to without aborting the entire transaction.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query and provides actual runtime statistics, whereas EXPLAIN alone shows the plan without execution.
The pgvector extension adds vector data types and indexing support for similarity search in PostgreSQL.
A partial index in PostgreSQL includes only the rows that meet the specified WHERE condition, reducing index size and improving performance for specific queries.
PostgreSQL implements SERIALIZABLE using Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI), which detects conflicts via predicate locks and transaction history rather than simply locking every row read.
HTTP status code 201 Created indicates that the request has been fulfilled and resulted in a new resource being created.
HTTP status code 204 No Content indicates a successful request where the server is not returning any content in the response body.
The HTTP specification defines DELETE as idempotent because multiple identical requests have the same effect on the server state.
The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is sent by the server in response to a request, not by the client.
HTTP status code 429 indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time, triggering rate limiting.
4xx codes indicate client errors, while 5xx codes indicate server-side errors.
The Content-Type header specifies the media type (MIME type) of the resource in the body.

RFC 5789 defines PATCH as a method that applies partial modifications, and unlike PUT, it is not required to be idempotent because the effect of applying the same patch multiple times may differ depending on the server's state.
Using == for hash comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks and loose type juggling issues; password_verify() or strict === should be used.
CSRF protection involves generating a unique token on the server, storing it in the user's session, and validating it upon submission of state-changing requests.
The Content-Security-Policy HTTP header is used to define the CSP policy for a web page.
OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework, not an authentication protocol; OpenID Connect is used for authentication.
XSS is primarily prevented by output encoding/escaping when rendering data, not just by input validation or database storage.
The authorization code is returned to the redirect_uri and exchanged for an access token.
Refresh tokens are designed to have longer lifespans than access tokens and are used to request new access tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate.
Password salts are typically stored in plaintext alongside the hash and do not need to be kept secret; their purpose is to prevent rainbow table attacks, not to hide information.
PHPUnit requires test classes to extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase (or implement the Test interface) to be recognized and executed.
setUp() runs before each individual test method, while setUpBeforeClass() runs once before all tests in the class.
A data provider can supply multiple sets of arguments, causing the test to run once for each set.
The expectException method is used to declare that a specific exception class should be thrown during the test.
In PHPUnit, a mock verifies that methods were called, while a stub only returns data.
PHPUnit 10 deprecated annotations in favor of PHP 8 attributes like #[DataProvider].
PHPUnit allows test dependencies using the @depends annotation.
The --order-by option with the value 'random' instructs PHPUnit to execute tests in a random order.
